name: Billerica
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Billerica, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Billerica, MA: the Town Common tree lighting with Santa, free Santa pictures, a Nutcracker class and trains from North Billerica.
lede: Billerica celebrates Christmas on its Town Common, where a volunteer festival group runs a free winter festival and tree lighting with Santa, and North Billerica sits right on the commuter rail line into Boston.
celebrates: Billerica's holiday season is built around the Town Common in Billerica Center. The Billerica Holiday Festival, an independent non-profit that offers free family events, runs a winter festival with games, crafts, cookies and hot chocolate before the annual tree lighting, when Santa and his friends arrive and the tree on the Common is switched on. Local churches and community groups add kids crafts and treats nearby. The festival group also hosts free pictures with Santa at the Senior Center and a Home for the Holidays display at the library, while the Billerica Police collect unwrapped toys for the Billerica Elks Giving Tree.
lastyear: In 2025 the Billerica Holiday Festival held its 27th Annual Tree Lighting on Saturday, December 6, on the Billerica Town Common, with Boston Bruins anthem singer Todd Angilly performing before Santa arrived and the tree was lit. One week later, on Saturday, December 13, 2025, the same volunteer group offered pictures with Santa from 10 am to 1:30 pm, part of its yearly lineup of family events in Billerica Center.
facts: Billerica was incorporated in 1655, on the same day as neighboring Chelmsford and nearby Groton. The settlers chose the name because some of the families came from Billericay in Essex, England. From 1795 to 1852 the Middlesex Canal flowed through town, carrying goods between Lowell and Boston. In 1877 Billerica also became one end of America's first two foot gauge common carrier railroad, the Billerica and Bedford.
trains: Billerica is a real train town. The Boston and Lowell Railroad's main line was built through North Billerica and East Billerica in the 1840s, and North Billerica station is still a stop on the MBTA Commuter Rail Lowell Line, so families can ride into Boston for holiday sights. On August 31, 1877, the Billerica and Bedford Railroad opened an 8.63 mile two foot gauge line with small steam engines named Ariel and Puck. For a Christmas train ride through the lights, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train.

kidfact: Billerica once had a tiny train with rails only two feet apart, the first railroad like it in America. Its two little steam engines were named Ariel and Puck.
faq: When is the Billerica tree lighting?

The Billerica Holiday Festival holds its tree lighting on the Town Common on a Saturday in early December. Afternoon festival games, crafts and treats come first, a singer and sing-along open the evening program, and Santa and his friends arrive just before the tree is lit. The 2025 lighting, the 27th, was on Saturday, December 6.
Is there a free place to get pictures with Santa in Billerica?

Yes. The Billerica Holiday Festival hosts free pictures with Santa at the Billerica Senior Center, 25 Concord Road in Billerica Center, on a Saturday in mid December. The 2025 session ran from 10 am to 1:30 pm. The group is an independent non-profit that offers free events for families.
Is there a train station in Billerica?

Yes. North Billerica station is a stop on the MBTA Commuter Rail Lowell Line, which runs between Lowell and Boston. The line follows the old Boston and Lowell Railroad, built through North Billerica and East Billerica in the 1840s. East Billerica stopped taking passengers in 1965, and that station is now a private home.
Where can kids donate toys at the Billerica tree lighting?

Billerica Police park a cruiser on the Council on Aging lawn during the tree lighting and collect unwrapped toys for the Billerica Elks Giving Tree, which helps children 12 and under. It is an easy way for kids to give a gift while they wait for Santa to arrive on the Common.
